Their mathematical dualism exposes a fundamental trade-off: individual psychologies excel at explaining variance but struggle with generalizability, while normative psychologies achieve robust predictions at the cost of ignoring person-specific nuance. Complete psychologies attempt reconciliation by conditioning responses on both stimulus and individual-event interactions. In GSI, this maps directly to Bayesian hierarchical models where individual-level random effects interact with covariates. In GSE, it informs multi-agent reinforcement learning with heterogeneous belief states.
